**Finding: missing (high severity) — no Customer termination for convenience.**

**What I found:**
- §8.1 sets a three-year term; §8.2 gives Order Forms auto-renewal with only a non-renewal opt-out.
- Section 9 (Termination) contains only cause-based rights: 9.1 material breach, 9.2 insolvency, 9.3 security/SLA/law/IP failures, and 9.5 (severability of Order Form terminations). There is no 9.4 and no convenience right for either party.
- §2.1 goes further and expressly locks Customer into USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights."
- Vendor has no convenience right either, so nothing needed to be deleted on that side; §24.4 already blocks a change-of-control exit for Vendor.

**Redline (validated, preferred position):**
1. New §9.4 after 9.3 — Customer may terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, on 30 days' written notice, without penalty or Fee acceleration, with refund of prepaid Fees per §10.2; Vendor expressly has no convenience/without-cause right during the term.
2. §2.1 — replaced "without reduction or termination rights" with language making the commitment subject to Customer's reduction and termination rights, including §9.4, so the take-or-pay clause cannot defeat the new exit right.

The comment flags the fallback (60–90 days' notice with an early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees) if Vendor resists 30 days, conditioned on Vendor taking no reciprocal walk-away.
